title: Today's top defense-tech headlines
big: 57 new stories since the last brief. The busiest areas: drones & air autonomy and allies & theaters.

stories.h: Space Nuclear Power Corporation Awarded DARPA Agreement for Ground Test of Autonomous Nuclear Reactor Controller
stories.what: LOS ALAMOS, N.M. — October 21, 2026 — Space Nuclear Power Corporation (SpaceNukes) announced today that the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) has awarded the company an Other Transaction [ ] The post Space Nuclear Power Corporation Awarded…
stories.you: More of the military's sensing and communications now runs through orbit, and new suppliers are getting in.

stories.h: Hegseth discusses Iran with Netanyahu in unannounced visit to Israel, officials say
stories.what: Netanyahu and Hegseth discussed “the threats in the region” and the U.S.-Israel partnership in dealing both offensively and defensively with those threats.
stories.you: Budget and policy moves decide which programs get real money and when; they're the earliest signal of demand.

stories.h: US Navy, Gecko Robotics surge AI maintenance contract to $300M
stories.what: Gecko Robotics uses drones, wall-climbing robots and fixed sensors to gather data on components, decks, welds and hulls.
stories.you: Software that decides what to look at and what to hit is where the most value is moving.

stories.h: Australia marks missile, cyber ‘firsts’ in exercise with Indonesia
stories.what: The Keris Woomera exercise comes during a busy month for Australia’s military, as forces participate in drills from Singapore to Japan.
stories.you: Weapons stockpiles are short, so anyone who can make missiles and rocket motors faster and cheaper has buyers.

stories.h: Britain’s cargo drone becomes a low-cost drone interceptor
stories.what: A heavy-lift cargo drone built by BAE Systems subsidiary Malloy Aeronautics has shot down several one-way attack drones with laser-guided rockets during a Pentagon experiment in Florida, firing one rocket after another without having to land and reload.
stories.you: Drones are becoming the military's default purchase, so volume, price and reliability decide who wins.

watch.why: Around November 3. Whether US commercial growth keeps outpacing government revenue.

idea.why: Sensor fusion and attribution software (RF, radar, acoustic, camera) for bases, data centers, stadiums, prisons and utilities. $14.4B FY27 counter-UAS line plus the base-defense pilot. Commercial sites legally can only detect and report drones, so software is what they buy.
